sentences.text: The name Metriacanthosaurus translates to 'moderately-spined lizard'.
This dinosaur was named for its neural spines, which are moderately tall compared to other theropods.
These neural spines are about 1.5 times the height of the centrum, a proportion similar to that seen in Megalosaurus, Sinraptor, and Ceratosaurus.
It was a medium-sized theropod with a femur measuring 80 cm in length.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight of Metriacanthosaurus at 1 tonne in 1988.
Thomas Holtz estimated the total length of the animal to be 8 meters.
Despite being little known, the name Metriacanthosaurus appears in one of the DNA tubes in the movie Jurassic Park.
The holotype specimen OUM J.12144 was discovered in 1871 by W. Parker at Jordan's Cliff near Weymouth, Dorset.
This fossil includes an incomplete pelvis, dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ten tail vertebrae, thigh bones, and an incomplete shin bone.
Friedrich von Huene described the fossils as a new species of Megalosaurus in 1923.
In 1932, Friedrich von Huene reclassified the species as Altispinax parkeri.
Alick Walker established the new genus Metriacanthosaurus in 1964 because the fossils lacked the long vertebral spines of Altispinax.
The generic name Metriacanthosaurus is derived from the Greek words for 'moderate' and 'spine'.
Metriacanthosaurus lived alongside other large theropods of the family Megalosauridae.
Metriacanthosaurus is classified within the family Metriacanthosauridae.
It is a member of the subfamily Metriacanthosaurinae.
This subfamily includes Metriacanthosaurus along with Sinraptor and Siamraptor.
Metriacanthosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 160 million years ago in the lower Oxfordian stage.
The fossil record for this animal spans from 161.5 to 159 million years ago within the Oxfordian stage.
A 2007 review by Darren Naish and David Martill argued that Metriacanthosaurus and Yangchuanosaurus should remain as separate genera.
